rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - no criminal record inquiry before conditional offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to complete a housing application with criminal record inquiries, or make any oral or written criminal record inquiry, before making a conditional offer. The provider may consider methamphetamine manufacture or production on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, other than units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units. A provider may consider whether an applicant was convicted of drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime sex offender registration requirement.
rules.penalty: Monetary penalty not to exceed $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 if one other violation within five years, and $10,000 if two or more other violations within seven years; the director may also order cease and desist, return of the application fee, and payment to the applicant up to $1,000.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - criminal history disclosure before application fee
rules.requirement: Before accepting any application fee, a housing provider must disclose in writing whether its eligibility criteria include review of criminal history and that the applicant may provide evidence of inaccuracies, rehabilitation or other mitigating factors.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - prohibited criminal record types
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not, before or after a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on arrests or charges without conviction, expunged convictions, pardoned convictions, vacated or nullified convictions, juvenile adjudications of delinquency, or sealed records.

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.penalty: Monetary penalty not to exceed $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 if one other violation within five years, and $10,000 if two or more other violations within seven years.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - lookback periods after conditional offer
rules.requirement: After a conditional offer, a housing provider may only consider convictions for listed serious offenses (including murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, and offenses requiring lifetime sex offender registration), first degree indictable offenses within six years, second or third degree within four years, and fourth degree within one year preceding the conditional offer.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - withdrawal of conditional offer
rules.requirement: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on criminal record only if it determines by preponderance of the evidence that withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest, after an individualized assessment; it must give written notice of the reasons and an opportunity to appeal, and on a request within 30 days must provide the relied-upon information free of charge within 10 days.

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.quoted_span: A housing provider may withdraw a conditional offer based on an applicant's criminal record only if the housing provider determines, by preponderance of the evidence, that the withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, and nondiscriminatory interest.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - discriminatory advertisements
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not knowingly or purposefully publish an advertisement stating it will not consider applicants who have been arrested or convicted of crimes, except as to methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, other than units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units; drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and lifetime sex offender registration.
rules.penalty: Monetary penalty not to exceed $1,000 for a first violation, $5,000 if one other violation within five years, and $10,000 if two or more other violations within seven years.
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not knowingly or purposefully publish, or cause to be published, any housing advertisement that explicitly provides that the housing provider will not consider any applicant who has been arrested or convicted of one or more crimes or offenses, except for drug-related criminal activity for the manufacture or production of methamphetamine on the premises of federally assisted housing, and whether the applicant is subject to a lifetime registration requirement under a State sex offender registration program.
rules.effective_date_phrase: This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment,

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act - drug and alcohol testing prohibited
rules.requirement: A housing provider may not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
rules.coverage_text: Housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes, other than units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not require an applicant to submit to a drug or alcohol test, or request the applicant’s consent to obtain information from a drug abuse treatment facility.
